title: Can the US Beat China’s Engineering State?

reader_summary.headline: I want people to get out of these rigid frameworks like socialists, capitalists.
reader_summary.overview: I want people to get out of these rigid frameworks like socialists, capitalists, neoliberal autocratic to think about the US and China. I want both Americans as well as Chinese to demand better from their government. What works really well in China, and what do we have in the US right now?

key_points.text: There is no winner here, there is no loser here, it's not a race, nobody gets a hit the win button.
key_points.evidence_quote: There is no winner here, there is no loser here, it's not a race, nobody gets a hit the win button.

key_points.text: We should be having some sort of better synthesis.
key_points.evidence_quote: We should be having some sort of better synthesis.

key_points.text: The US and China aren't just competing on technology, they're competing on how to build.
key_points.evidence_quote: The US and China aren't just competing on technology, they're competing on how to build.

key_points.text: In today's episode, I'm joined by Dan Wang, author of The New York Times Best Seller Breakneck.
key_points.evidence_quote: In today's episode, I'm joined by Dan Wang, author of The New York Times Best Seller Breakneck.

thesis: The episode argues that the US and China are competing on how to build, contrasting the US as a lawyer-led society with China as an engineer-led state. The speakers advocate for a synthesis where the US adopts China's functional logistical and urban systems while China respects individual rights and entrepreneurial drive.
